feature: Saved audio PCM frame and tail conservation

scenarios.name: Converted files retain their final audio samples
scenarios.given: a saved mono 16kHz PCM file, stored as either Float32 or signed Int16, ends in a short buffer with distinctive final samples
scenarios.when: the raw file feed converts it to mono Int16 or reads matching Float32 without conversion and reaches EOF
scenarios.then: every source frame and the distinctive tail are emitted once, EOF remains stable, and the saved file bytes are unchanged

scenarios.name: Drained chunk tails preserve recording time
scenarios.given: three saved PCM chunks stored as Float32 or signed Int16 overlap or have a real timeline gap
scenarios.when: the converted chunks are read sequentially through EOF
scenarios.then: all frames including each tail precede the next chunk, only first buffers carry anchors, overlap starts at the fully emitted preceding end and real gaps remain

scenarios.name: Cancelling a feed suppresses its pending tail
scenarios.given: a saved Float32 or signed Int16 PCM file has observable final audio still undelivered and another chunk follows
scenarios.when: the feed is stopped before the remaining audio is requested
scenarios.then: no further PCM or next chunk is returned, cancellation preserves source bytes, and a supplied first failure remains observable

scenarios.name: Empty and unreadable saved files end safely
scenarios.given: a file feed has no chunks, a valid zero-frame file, or an unreadable or invalid file
scenarios.then: empty inputs end without invented samples, read errors are retained and prevent later chunks from being read, and no source is modified
